text:
Alex: seeing a sharp p95 jump across GPU nodes in us-west-2 during our peak batching window, started ~10:32am. p95 went from ~35ms -> 360ms, tails up to ~700ms. Feels like a peer-handoff/handshake flare between nodes.
Sera: any packet loss counters or RDMA retries visible?
Alex: yes, saw sporadic RXE retransmits on a subset of nodes. quick paste from `ethtool -S ens1f0`:
```
rx_missed: 132
rx_crc_errors: 9
tx_restart: 0
rx_nohandler: 18
```
Maria: we rolled a TOR firmware change late last night for rack-e. can we confirm MTU/auto-neg across NICs in that rack?
Raj: running iperf3 between gpu-a01 and gpu-a12 now, will post numbers.
ops-bot: NOTE: BGP flapping alert in us-west-2 affected a handful of spines at 10:25, alert cleared at 10:28.
Raj: iperf3 snapshot during spike: 9.8 Gbits/sec overall but jitter jumped from 1.2ms -> 32ms and packet loss ~0.12% for short bursts.
Sera: that pattern matches large-packet coalescence delaying small RDMA control pkts during batch bursts. check driver tx_coalesce / rx_coalesce timers and NIC interrupt moderation.
Alex: temporary mitigation: reduced max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 on canary hosts; p95 improved back to ~75ms for those canaries.
Maria: isolate racks that had the firmware tweak and revert if metrics degrade. we should also check if any MTU was auto-negotiated down to 1500.
Raj: opened CASE-4821 with vendor, attached packet captures and ethtool dumps. reference in ticket: tcpreplay of the capture reproduces the jitter on kit.
Alex: plan: keep reduced batch on 50% of serving capacity, run deeper NIC counters at 16:00, and collect RDMA retry histograms.
Sera: add alert rule: rxe_retries > 20/min => trigger auto-fallback to smaller batch size and route traffic to unaffected racks.
Maria: +1. ops-bot, can you kick a canary config rollout for the batch-size change?
ops-bot: starting canary rollout to 10% of fleet now :rocket: (config: max_batch_size=32 on canary groups)
Alex: thanks — monitoring dashboards updated. will escalate to network oncall if spike returns. tagging @network-oncall and leaving the vendor ticket open.
